verdict.reasoning: Patient reports shortness of breath, cough and feeling feverish for several days and has a history of asthma: "I have feel like kind of shorter breath" for "2, 3 days"; "I have cough... and I have a fever"; "Yes, I had asthma."
Duration and exertional nature stated: "So recently I'm busy. I have feel like kind of shorter breath" and when asked how long: "2, 3 days"; later specifies on walking: "Just walk...".
Patient states reduced walking ability: "I also used to walk to work, but recently I can't because... I feel like very short of breath" and has been working from home or on sick leave.
Explicitly described: "sometimes I feel like I can't even finish top saying a sentence. It's quite difficult to... complete the... talking sometimes."

Patient says both that they have a fever and that their home temperature was 37°C and normal: "I have... a fever" but later "Was it normal?" "Yeah"; "What Was your temperature?" "37. Yeah." The fact states they report a fever with 37°C, which is not how they frame it when giving the value (they call it normal).
Patient reports cough without sputum: "Have you coughed any phlegm up or anything like that?" "No."
Denial of chest pain: "Any chest pain?" "No chest pain? No."
Denial of hemoptysis: "Any, any blood in there when you cough?" "No, I don't think so."
No nocturnal symptoms: "Have you been woken up at night time at all?" "No. Just daytime walking?"
States inability to exercise: when asked "Have you been able to do any exercise?" patient responds "No, I can't."
Previously walked to work and now mainly at home: "I also used to walk to work, but recently I work from home or sometimes I take sick leave."
History of childhood asthma: asked about childhood wheeze/asthma: "Yes, I had asthma..." and discussion of severity and missing school as a child.
Hay fever history: "I also had hay fever and asthma eczema as well" and later "I have hay fever as well."
Eczema history: "I also had hay fever and asthma eczema as well."
Regular inhaler use in past childhood: "Did you have to take medication?" "Yeah, I take the asthma inhaler."

Transcript indicates ongoing reliever use over last 3–4 years: "when do you think that asthma stopped?... Few years ago. Like three or four years ago" (re: not taking medication as a child). Later: "How about the last three to four years?" "Yeah." "Have you taken any medication?" "I took sulbutomal. Yeah." and “Normally, yeah.” So they have been on salbutamol during that period.

Current as-needed salbutamol: "Have you taken any medication?" "I took sulbutomal. Yeah." and "Okay, so you, you normally take that, do you or is that just recently?" "Normally, yeah." and current plan involves using their inhaler more regularly, implying current possession/use.

No spacer at home: When asked "Have you got a spacer at home?" patient implies none, and doctor responds with plan to prescribe one; patient does not contradict and later says "No" when asked initially about spacer: "Do you have a spacer at home?" "No."
No peak flow meter at home: "Do you have a peak flow meter at home..." "No. No."
No allergies: "Any allergies to medications?" "No, no allergies."
Non-smoker: "Do you smoke?" "No, I don't smoke."
Alcohol intake: "Do you drink any alcohol regularly?" "Yeah, one glass." then clarifies "One glass of wine... Every two or three days. Depends."
Living situation: "Who do you live with? Do you live on your own or do you live with." "I live with my partner."
Occupation: "What's your job day to day?" "I'm an engineer."
Working from home recently: "have you been at work in the last few days?" "No, I can't because I used to walk to work, but recently I work from home or sometimes I take sick leave."
Afebrile by home check 37°C: "Did you say you checked your temperature already?" "Yes, I checked." "Was it normal?" "Yeah"; "What Was your temperature?" "37. Yeah."
No chest pain on ROS: "Any chest pain?" "No chest pain? No."
No syncope is never discussed in the transcript; there is no mention of fainting or blackouts.
No nocturnal symptoms: "Have you been woken up at night time at all?" "No. Just daytime walking?"
37°C was a home measurement, not a clinic vital: "Did you say you checked your temperature already?... What Was your temperature?" "37. Yeah." There is no in-clinic temperature documented.
No vitals or exam findings besides reported home temperature are documented in the transcript; there is no pulse, BP, RR, SpO2, or physical exam noted.
Doctor’s assessment: "it sounds like you've had a flare up of your asthma" and symptoms are exertional: shortness of breath "Just walk" and reduced ability to walk to work.

History of childhood-onset asthma and no regular controller: childhood asthma discussed; current meds only salbutamol reliever, no preventer inhaler mentioned; doctor suggests "we may need to start some other medications for you," implying absence of controller now.
Hay fever/allergic rhinitis history: "I also had hay fever" and later "I have hay fever as well."
Only objective figure is home temperature; no vitals, peak flow, or auscultation documented: doctor plans to prescribe peak flow meter; no exam findings in transcript.
Peak flow meter prescription: "I can prescribe you a peak flow meter so we can check your breathing level."
Spacer prescription: "and a spacer to use your inhaler a bit more efficiently, which the pharmacist can show you how you use that when you pick it up."

Instruction to increase inhaler to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours: "if you increase it so you're taking it two to four puffs, like every four hours initially" and this is in the context of using the spacer once prescribed.
Regular antihistamine plan: "the other thing to do would be to take a regular antihistamine, which you can get from the pharmacy. I can put a suggestion on your notes about what to take."

Reassessment in about a week to consider other meds: "it would be a good idea, when you're feeling better, if we could arrange just a review... we may need to start some other medications for you" and "You can arrange a review in a week or so."

Safety net advice only mentions high temperature or worsening wheeze: "if you get a high temperature or your wheezing is getting worse, you need to call us back straight away." There is no mention of inability to speak in full sentences or seeking urgent care beyond calling back.

Peak flow recording instruction: "if you could record a value first thing when you wake up in the evening over the next week. And then we can discuss that over the phone when we look at the figures." (intended: morning and evening for a week).
Pharmacist demonstration: "a spacer... which the pharmacist can show you how you use that when you pick it up."
Doctor says "I can put a suggestion on your notes about what to take" for antihistamine, but there is no statement that written notes for home use and follow-up plan will be given to the patient.
Plan to consider escalation if control poor: "we may need to start some other medications for you" and will review after seeing peak flow and symptoms, implying escalation if needed.
Follow-up in about one week: "You can arrange a review in a week or so." and patient repeats "Yeah, a week. Right. Okay."
Discuss peak flow results by phone: "if you could record a value... over the next week. And then we can discuss that over the phone when we look at the figures."
